statement_record.book: A category J is finite when it has finitely many morphisms; a footnote observes that J then has finitely many objects too, since every object contributes its own identity morphism.
statement_record.intree: Record Metacategory := { arr := nat; pairs : M.t arr; ... } together with FromArrows (M : Metacategory) : Category := {| obj := ∃ i : arr M, identity M i; hom := fun x y => ∃ f : arr M, defined f ``x (pairs M) ∧ defined ``y f (pairs M) |} and cardinality M := M.cardinal (P.filter (identity-entries) (pairs M)).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: finiteness is a PRESENTATION (a category built from a finite composition table), not a PREDICATE on an arbitrary category. Nothing in-tree asserts of a given [J : Category] that its morphisms are finite in number, and nothing proves the footnote's implication morphisms-finite ⇒ objects-finite. The footnote's identification of objects with identity arrows IS realized, both as [FromArrows]'s [obj := ∃ i, identity M i] and as [cardinality]'s filter on identity entries.

gap: No finiteness predicate on categories exists: there is no [FiniteCategory J], no [Finite]/[IsFinite] class, and no lemma 'J has finitely many morphisms → J has finitely many objects'. What exists is (a) concrete finite index categories used as limit/colimit shapes — [_0] (Instance/Zero.v), [_1] (Instance/One.v), [Two_Discrete], [Roof] (Instance/Roof.v), [Parallel] (Instance/Parallel.v) — none carrying a finiteness certificate, and (b) the arrows-only [Metacategory] presentation, whose [pairs] is a finite map and whose [cardinality] counts identity arrows, but whose induced [FromArrows] hom type is a subtype of [nat] that is never proved finite. Consequently Definition 6.30's quantification 'for every finite J' cannot be expressed.

The FIRST half is VACUOUS. Metacategory.v:157-158 defines identity u := (forall f : arr, composite f u f) /\ (forall g : arr, composite u g g) with NO definedness guard, over arr := nat; since pairs : M.t arr is a finite map, no u can satisfy it. This is already proved in-tree by the audit probe doc/plan/books/probes/S8-metacategory-vacuity.v (identity_unsatisfiable, FromArrows_no_objects, Three_is_empty), and the file's own comment at :146-156 wrongly claims the guard-free encoding 'is sound for the finite, explicitly-enumerated metacategories built here'. What survives as PARTIAL evidence is therefore only: (a) the Metacategory record itself, whose pairs : M.t arr IS genuine finite data (a category presented by a finite composition table), and (b) cardinality + ThreeArrows_card_3, a syntactic count of the (i,i) |-> i table entries that is independent of the unsatisfiable identity predicate and does compute. Two further caveats the record should have named: Metacategory is declared inside the module functor `Module Metacategory (M : WSfun PNN)` (Metacategory.v:121) which the library never applies outside its own file, and the file's own header at :112-115 states 'The module stands apart from the working library: nothing in Instance/, Construction/ or Structure/ depends on it.' Note the parallel Theory/Metacategory/ArrowsOnly.v keeps the conditional guard and is NOT vacuous; it was not cited but is the healthier witness.
